g.text: What a visitor does from the first page to the confirmation.
Every event, its date and seats left.
That one event, and how full it is.
Asks to join the waiting list
Joins the queue; the message is written.
moves up by itself when somebody gives up a seat
Recounts, so the last seat is not sold twice.
Booking, history and e-mail, all at once.
the e-mail is sent on sheet C
Online Event Registration System · sheet A of 3 · regenerate with python3 docs/generate-diagrams.py
B · Administration — what the organizer does
Sign in, read the counters, then edit an event, check people in, or change a booking.
Matches it against the one on file.
Stays signed in, so it is not asked again.
Counts events, booked seats, waiting and arrivals.
Saves it, or hides it from the public list.
Marks them arrived, notes who did it.
Frees the seat and offers it to the next one waiting.
every change above is also kept in the history, and sends its message
Online Event Registration System · sheet B of 3 · regenerate with python3 docs/generate-diagrams.py
C · Sending the mail, and the guest manage link
Mail goes out in the background, so a broken mailbox never breaks a booking.
Fills in the template, then sends it
Retries up to three times, then marks it failed.
the Requeue button sends it again at once
Notes that it went out, and when.
that link came from sheet A
Finds the person and booking; checks it is still valid.
Sees the booking: event, date, place
Same as the signed-in page: seat freed, next one offered it.
Saves it and marks the link as used.
